steps.title: Instrument cleaning and setup
steps.instruction: Turn on the BD FACSCanto II, run the cleaning mode and clean the slit, flow cell and flow tubes using the FACS clean solution and FACS flow sheath as described in the instrument manual.

steps.title: Instrument calibration with beads
steps.instruction: Calibrate the cytometer using BD OneFlow setup beads and BD FACSDiva CS&T research beads.

substeps.instruction: Mix one drop of BD OneFlow setup beads in 500 µL sheath fluid.
Mix one drop of FACSDiva CS&T research beads in a separate 500 µL sheath fluid.

steps.title: Sheath‑fluid wash between samples
steps.instruction: Before loading a new sample, run sheath fluid through the sample injection port for at least 1 minute to prevent cross‑sample contamination.

steps.title: Collect peripheral blood sample
steps.instruction: Draw 3 mL of peripheral whole blood with a 23‑gauge needle and syringe, transfer it into a K2‑EDTA vacutainer tube and gently invert 3–4 times; centrifuge the tube for plasma separation within 4 hours of collection.

steps.title: Prepare platelet‑free plasma
steps.instruction: Process the EDTA blood to obtain platelet‑free plasma (PFP) by sequential centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge 2 mL of the blood at 400 × g for 15 min at room temperature.
Transfer the supernatant to a plastic round‑bottom tube, leaving ~500 µL above the buffy coat (discard pellet and buffy coat).
Centrifuge the transferred supernatant at 2,000 × g for 15 min at room temperature.
Transfer the new supernatant, leaving ~100 µL behind.
Centrifuge again at 2,000 × g for 15 min.
Aliquot the final supernatant, leaving ~100 µL behind; this aliquot is the PFP.

steps.title: Set PMT voltages and scatter
steps.instruction: Adjust the flow cytometer for EV detection using unstained PFP as a baseline and set the voltages as specified.

substeps.instruction: Place 100 µL of unstained PFP from a healthy donor into a 5 mL acquisition tube (control).
In a second tube, add 100 µL PFP, then add 2 µL each of CD41A, CD62P, CD62E and CD235a antibodies.
Incubate both tubes in the dark for 20 min at room temperature.
Add 500 µL sheath fluid to each tube and mix gently.
Switch the cytometer to high‑sensitivity mode, use logarithmic scaling for FSC and SSC, and calibrate with 100 nm, 200 nm and 500 nm size‑standard beads.
Set the following voltages: FSC = 375 V; SSC = 373 V; APC‑H7 = 558 V; BV421 = 416 V; PE = 432 V; APC = 508 V. Keep these settings unchanged for the whole experiment.

steps.title: Create compensation controls
steps.instruction: Prepare single‑color compensation controls using UltraComp eBeads.

substeps.instruction: Vortex the compensation beads for 30 seconds.
Label four Falcon tubes C1–C4 and add two drops of beads to each tube.
Add 100 µL protein‑free PBS to each tube.
Add 1 µL of the appropriate antibody to each tube: C1 = CD235a, C2 = CD41a, C3 = CD62P, C4 = CD62E.
Mix well and incubate in the dark for 10 min at room temperature.
Wash the beads with PBS and centrifuge at 800 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend the bead pellet in 200 µL PBS and run the compensation on the BD FACSCanto II.

steps.title: Create FMO controls
steps.instruction: Prepare fluorescence‑minus‑one (FMO) tubes to define gating boundaries.

substeps.instruction: Prepare five 5 mL acquisition tubes as follows (add 100 µL PFP to each):
FMO 1: add 2 µL CD41a, 2 µL CD62P, 2 µL CD62E (no CD235a).
FMO 2: add 2 µL CD235a, 2 µL CD62P, 2 µL CD62E (no CD41a).
FMO 3: add 2 µL CD41a, 2 µL CD235a, 2 µL CD62E (no CD62P).
FMO 4: add 2 µL CD41a, 2 µL CD235a, 2 µL CD62P (no CD62E).
Plasma sample (full panel): add 2 µL each of CD41a, CD235a, CD62P and CD62E.
Incubate all tubes in the dark for 20 min at room temperature.
Add 500 µL sheath fluid to each tube and mix gently.

steps.title: Acquire FMO data
steps.instruction: Run each FMO tube on the cytometer and collect at least 30 000 EV events per tube.

substeps.instruction: Set the sample flow rate to a medium setting and the flow pressure to 2.83 × 10⁴ Pa.
Acquire ≥30 000 events using BD FACSDiva software v8.0.3.
Apply SSC‑A vs FSC‑A gating to identify the EV population, then FSC‑A vs FSC‑H gating to exclude doublets.

steps.title: Prepare experimental sample
steps.instruction: Stain the PFP sample with the full antibody panel for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 100 µL PFP into a 5 mL acquisition tube.
Add 2 µL each of CD41A, CD62P, CD62E and CD235a antibodies.
Incubate in the dark for 20 min at room temperature.
Add 500 µL sheath fluid and mix gently (no washing steps).

steps.title: Acquire experimental data
steps.instruction: Collect EV events from the stained sample and perform gating.

substeps.instruction: Run the sample on the BD FACSCanto II with the flow rate set to medium and pressure to 2.83 × 10⁴ Pa.
Acquire 30 000 positive events using BD FACSDiva software v8.0.3.
Apply SSC‑A vs FSC‑A gating to define the EV population and FSC‑A vs FSC‑H gating to remove doublets.

description: Validation of protocol This flow cytometry protocol for the analysis of EVs in blood has been used in an ongoing study of patients with snakebite-associated thrombotic microangiopathy. To ensure reproducibility and reliability of this protocol, we undertook several validation measures. FMO and controls were performed to accurately define EV populations. 20 healthy control samples were analyzed in batch to establish baseline MV isolation patterns in normal controls. In total, we examined 35 patient samples across different clinical presentations, and for each patient sample batch analyzed, a normal control was included in parallel. All acquisitions were performed by the same researcher using the same flow cytometer (BD FACS Canto II) and standardized consumables (same batch of blood collection tubes, syringes, centrifuge, and reagents) to minimize both inter-operator and instrument-to-instrument variability. This standardized approach reduced potential technical variation and increased confidence in biological differences observed. Statistical analyses were performed using GraphPad Prism/SPSS to compare EV counts among groups (healthy controls and patients), showing significant differences consistent with disease pathology. EV profiles of a control and a patient are included in Figure S2. Notably, endothelial EVs (CD62E + ) and red cell EVs (CD235a + ) were significantly elevated in snakebite patients compared to controls (median red cell EVs 63.2 vs. 26.2, p < 0.05; median endothelial EVs 40.6 vs. 4.3, p < 0.05), suggesting that endothelial injury plays a central role in its pathophysiology. These findings are currently being prepared for submission in a separate research manuscript. Although the associated research article has not yet been published, the protocol has been applied in a clinical research study supported by the South Asian Clinical Toxicology Research Collaboration, Sri Lanka (SACTRC).
